boe-rate.name: Bank of England Bank Rate
boe-rate.description: Official Bank Rate, time-weighted annual mean. Counters the 'rates were 15% in the 80s' rebuttal.

source.name: Bank of England via datahub.io mirror

house-price-landreg.name: House prices (HM Land Registry, UK)
house-price-landreg.description: UK average property price from the official UK HPI, monthly aggregated to annual mean. Methodology dates from 1968.

source.name: HM Land Registry UK House Price Index

house-price-london.name: House prices (London)
house-price-london.description: Greater London average property price, UK HPI monthly → annual mean. The methodology cliff that the UK average hides.

source.name: HM Land Registry UK House Price Index

house-price-northeast.name: House prices (North East)
house-price-northeast.description: North East England average property price. The opposite end of the same chart — the cheapest English region.

source.name: HM Land Registry UK House Price Index

house-price-nationwide.name: House prices (Nationwide HPI)
house-price-nationwide.description: UK Nationwide House Price Index, quarterly from Feb 1953. Aggregated to annual mean of the 'Price (All)' column. Methodology differs from Land Registry HPI — included for the longer back-series.

source.name: Nationwide via datahub.io mirror

cpih.name: Inflation (CPIH)
cpih.description: ONS Consumer Prices Index including owner-occupier housing costs, 2015 = 100. National Statistic 1988+; pre-1988 are ONS modelled historical estimates rebased to the modern 2015 base via the 1988 overlap. Pre-1988 portion is officially flagged as 'not National Statistics' by ONS.

source.name: ONS — CPIH (l522/mm23) + Consumer Price Inflation historical 1950 to 1988

median-wage.name: Median wage (full-time, annual)
median-wage.description: UK median gross annual pay, adult full-time employees. Weekly ONS NES/ASHE figures × 52. Combined male+female median is published from 1984 onwards. For 1968-1983 we use the Adult Male median scaled by the male-to-combined ratio at 1984 (proxy, since combined wasn't published in the NES era).

source.name: ONS — earnings time series of median gross weekly earnings 1968 to latest

household-income.name: Household disposable income (per head)
household-income.description: UK gross disposable household income per head, current price £, seasonally adjusted. The 'how much does each person have to play with after tax' line — useful counterweight to wages.

source.name: ONS — Household disposable income per head (CRXS)

energy-cost.name: Energy (typical dual-fuel annual bill)
energy-cost.description: Typical UK household annual dual-fuel bill (nominal £). 2019+ is the Ofgem default tariff cap (April-level each year); 2022/2023 reflect the effective EPG-capped cost. Pre-2019 uses DESNZ Quarterly Energy Prices averages; pre-1980 are rough nominal estimates (coal-and-town-gas era, not directly comparable to today's bills).

source.name: Ofgem default tariff cap + DESNZ Quarterly Energy Prices + historical estimates

rent-index.name: Private rent index (UK)
rent-index.description: UK private rental price index, 2015 = 100. 2005+ from ONS IPHRP / PIPR (official). Pre-2005 estimated from survey data: the previous splice of the RPI housing-rent component overstated historical rents ~2× because the RPI component tracked sitting-tenant rents (many regulated under the Rent Acts) rather than market-rate private lets. The revised pre-2005 values are calibrated to ONS/EHS survey evidence that private renters spent ~29% of income on rent in 1993 (the anchor point), implying 1990 market-rate rent ≈ £300-320/month — vs the old splice's implied £520/month which was plainly wrong.

source.name: ONS — IPHRP/PIPR (2005+); EHS/survey calibration (pre-2005)

netflix-uk.name: Netflix UK Standard plan (annual)
netflix-uk.description: Annual cost of Netflix UK Standard plan (monthly price × 12). Tiers were reshuffled in 2024 — values use the modal Standard tier of each year. Included tongue-in-cheek because the original 'avocado toast and Netflix' rhetoric named it.

source.name: Netflix UK pricing history (press releases + archived plan pages)

avocado-uk.name: Avocado (single supermarket avg)
avocado-uk.description: Approximate UK supermarket avocado retail price per unit. ⚠️ No clean canonical source — values are based on retail surveys and archived supermarket listings, included for the joke. Treat as illustrative.

source.name: Mixed retail surveys / archived supermarket listings

birth-rate.name: Crude birth rate (per 1,000)
birth-rate.description: UK live births per 1,000 population. The fertility floor — 2023 was the lowest on record (9.5).

source.name: ONS — Births in England and Wales (UK aggregate)

net-migration.name: Net long-term international migration
net-migration.description: UK net long-term international migration, thousands of people. 2012+ uses the ONS admin-data methodology; pre-2012 uses the legacy IPS-based estimates (not strictly comparable). Pre-1990 values are decadal estimates from House of Commons Library research.

source.name: ONS — Long-term international migration (+ HoC Library pre-1990 estimates)

persons-per-household.name: Persons per household (avg)
persons-per-household.description: Average UK household size from census + ONS Families and Households. Slow-moving but unmistakable downward trend: more solo earners absorbing the costs that used to be split.

source.name: ONS — Families and households / UK Census + General Register Office (pre-1961)

tuition-uk.name: Undergraduate tuition fees (England, max)
tuition-uk.description: Maximum annual undergraduate tuition fee chargeable by English universities. Pre-1998 = £0 (no fees). Top-up fees raised the cap to £3,000 in 2006; the Browne reforms tripled it to £9,000 in 2012. Held flat at £9,250 since 2017.

source.name: Department for Education / Office for Students fee cap history

council-tax.name: Council Tax (England, Band D average)
council-tax.description: Average council tax bill for a Band D property in England. Council tax replaced the community charge in 1993. Pre-1993 figures show domestic rates / community charge equivalents for context (modelled, dashed).

source.name: Department for Levelling Up, Housing & Communities / MHCLG council-tax statistics

rail-fares.name: Rail fares (UK index, Jan 1995 = 100)
rail-fares.description: ORR/DfT rail-fares index covering all GB rail tickets. Regulated fares track RPI (+1% for many years post-2004) — the line climbs faster than wages essentially by formula. Pre-1995 indexed back to BR-era estimates (dashed).

source.name: Office of Rail and Road — Rail fares index

min-wage.name: Minimum / National Living Wage (annual, 37.5h)
min-wage.description: Statutory wage floor for adults (21/22+), annualised at a 37.5-hour week × 52 weeks. National Minimum Wage introduced 1999 at £3.60; rebadged National Living Wage for 25+ from 2016 and lowered to 21+ from 2024. Pre-1999 there was no UK statutory floor.

source.name: Low Pay Commission / gov.uk NMW & NLW rates

student-debt.name: Student loan balance at graduation (England, average)
student-debt.description: Average outstanding student-loan balance on the day of graduation, England, full-time undergrad. Combines tuition-fee loans and maintenance loans. Reflects 3 years of borrowing under each year's regime. Pre-1998 = £0 (no tuition fees, mortgage-style maintenance loans were small).

source.name: Student Loans Company / House of Commons Library — Student loan statistics

childcare-cost.name: Full-time nursery (England, under-2, annual)
childcare-cost.description: Annual cost of full-time (50h/week) nursery for a child under 2 in England. Coram Family & Childcare conducts the canonical annual survey; nominal £, sticker price (before any government support). Pre-2003 modelled from CPI-trended estimates of historical part-time rates (dashed).

source.name: Coram Family & Childcare — Childcare Survey

homeownership-25-34.name: Homeownership rate (25–34)
homeownership-25-34.description: Share of household reference persons in this age band who own their home (with or without a mortgage). Compiled from the English Housing Survey / ONS LFS / Census tenure tables.

source.name: ONS / English Housing Survey — Tenure by age

homeownership-35-44.name: Homeownership rate (35–44)
homeownership-35-44.description: Share of household reference persons in this age band who own their home (with or without a mortgage). Compiled from the English Housing Survey / ONS LFS / Census tenure tables.

source.name: ONS / English Housing Survey — Tenure by age

homeownership-55-64.name: Homeownership rate (55–64)
homeownership-55-64.description: Share of household reference persons in this age band who own their home (with or without a mortgage). Compiled from the English Housing Survey / ONS LFS / Census tenure tables.

source.name: ONS / English Housing Survey — Tenure by age

ftb-age.name: First-time buyer average age (UK)
ftb-age.description: Average age of UK first-time buyers based on mortgage completions. Combines HMRC / CML / UK Finance / Halifax FTB tracker historical figures. Pre-1995 reflects industry estimates (dashed).

source.name: UK Finance / Halifax First-Time Buyer Review

tax-burden-median.name: Effective tax + NI rate (median earner)
tax-burden-median.description: Income tax + employee National Insurance as a percentage of gross pay for a single worker on the median full-time wage. Reflects each year's personal allowance, basic-rate threshold and NI primary threshold. Pre-1990 modelled from IFS historical effective-rate tables (dashed).

source.name: HMRC / IFS — Direct tax statistics

grad-salary.name: Graduate starting salary (median, UK)
grad-salary.description: Median annual starting salary for new UK graduates entering full-time employment. Combines HECSU 'What Do Graduates Do?' and ISE Student Recruitment Survey medians. Nominal £.

source.name: HECSU / Prospects + Institute of Student Employers

food-cpi.name: Food & drink price index (CPIH)
food-cpi.description: ONS CPIH food and non-alcoholic beverages sub-index, 2015 = 100. Food rose ~39% from 2015 to 2023, vs 29% for CPIH overall — the 2022-23 cost-of-living spike was disproportionately a food crisis. Pre-2005 estimated from RPI food component.

source.name: ONS — CPIH food & non-alcoholic beverages sub-index

wage-p25.name: Lower quartile wage (full-time, annual)
wage-p25.description: UK lower quartile (P25) gross annual pay, adult full-time employees. Based on ONS ASHE Table 1 annual history.

source.name: ONS — Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) Table 1

wage-p75.name: Upper quartile wage (full-time, annual)
wage-p75.description: UK upper quartile (P75) gross annual pay, adult full-time employees. Based on ONS ASHE Table 1 annual history.

source.name: ONS — Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) Table 1

fuel-price.name: Petrol pump price (pence per litre)
fuel-price.description: Annual average UK unleaded petrol pump price (pence per litre). Pre-2000 estimated from BEIS historical data; solid from 2000.

source.name: BEIS / RAC Foundation — UK average unleaded pump price

wealth-25-34.name: Median household wealth, age 25–34
wealth-25-34.description: Median total net household wealth (nominal £) for households headed by someone aged 25–34. ONS Wealth & Assets Survey biennial waves.

source.name: ONS — Wealth & Assets Survey

wealth-55-64.name: Median household wealth, age 55–64
wealth-55-64.description: Median total net household wealth (nominal £) for households headed by someone aged 55–64. ONS Wealth & Assets Survey biennial waves.

source.name: ONS — Wealth & Assets Survey

healthcare-oop.name: NHS out-of-pocket costs (dental + prescriptions)
healthcare-oop.description: Annual out-of-pocket NHS costs for a typical working-age adult: 12 prescription items + 2 dental check-ups + 1 Band 2 treatment. Pre-2000 NHS was effectively free at point of use for most; charges have risen above inflation since. Figures exclude private healthcare.

source.name: NHS England — prescription charge history; NHS dental charge bands

public-sector-wage.name: Median wage — public sector
public-sector-wage.description: ONS ASHE median full-time weekly earnings, public sector employees. Includes NHS, teaching, civil service etc.

source.name: ONS ASHE — sector breakdown

private-sector-wage.name: Median wage — private sector
private-sector-wage.description: ONS ASHE median full-time weekly earnings, private sector employees.

source.name: ONS ASHE — sector breakdown

intl-hpw-uk.name: UK house-price-to-median-wage ratio
intl-hpw-uk.description: Years of median gross annual wage required to purchase the average home. Derived from OECD housing price data and national median wage statistics. Pre-verifiedFrom points are modelled estimates.

source.name: OECD / national statistics (modelled)

intl-hpw-germany.name: Germany house-price-to-median-wage ratio
intl-hpw-germany.description: Years of median gross annual wage required to purchase the average home. Derived from OECD housing price data and national median wage statistics. Pre-verifiedFrom points are modelled estimates.

source.name: OECD / national statistics (modelled)

intl-hpw-canada.name: Canada house-price-to-median-wage ratio
intl-hpw-canada.description: Years of median gross annual wage required to purchase the average home. Derived from OECD housing price data and national median wage statistics. Pre-verifiedFrom points are modelled estimates.

source.name: OECD / national statistics (modelled)
